(1) the SCM provides a unified theory of causation; (2) the SCM can be used to answer queries of type (1) and (3); and (3) the SCM can answer queries of type(2) if and only if the query involves a set of variables that satisfies the back-door criterion

the following three statements are true: (a) the effect of an action is the difference between the observed and counterfactual outcomes; (b) the counterfactual outcome can be expressed as a function of the observed outcome and the structural equation that describes the action; and (c) the structural equation can be estimated from a mixture of experimental, observational, and instrumental data.

(1) the SCM provides a unified theory of causality, (2) the SCM provides tools to infer the answers to three different types of causal queries, (3) the SCM is a generalization of the structural equations approach to causal analysis, and (4) the SCM is compatible with the potential outcome approach to causal analysis.
